videos.title: DLSS 5 explained, with Linus Tech Tips | The Vergecast
videos.description:
Nvidia's new DLSS 5 (Deep Learning Super Sampling 5) rendering technology uses AI to (theoretically) improve video game graphics. When it was announced, social media declared that it was "yassifying" video game characters, changing faces in a way game developers didn't intend. Linus Tech Tips' own Linus Sebastian and David Gauthier join guest host David Imel to break down the the hype and controversy.

videos.description: Steam Machine gets snap-on screens. The JSAUX E-Ink Faceplate and Pixel Matrix Faceplate magnetically snap onto Valve's living room game console, giving you a 640 x 480 black-and-white canvas (or 64 x 54 for color dot-matrix) to play with. They come with all kinds of tradeoffs and compromises, but they work, and the e-paper screen has a battery and Bluetooth inside so it doesn't always need plugged in. videos.title: Googlebooks are coming for your Mac | The Vergecast
videos.description:
We tried out the new Googlebooks, which are essentially Chromebooks evolved with an Android elemental stone. They're made by Dell, Lenovo, HP, Acer, and Asus (not Google), but all have the new Googlebook OS, heavy Android phone and Gemini integration, and a built-in "Glowbar." Laptop reviewer Antonio G. Di Benedetto went hands-on with the new devices, and reports back to guest host David Imel.

videos.title: First look at Googlebook
videos.description:
Google is launching a whole new line of laptops called Googlebooks. They’re similar to Chromebooks, but they run on Android instead of ChromeOS. Which means they’re far more integrated with your Android phone than other laptops. Five new Googlebooks launch October 4th, starting at $899. Is that exciting enough to get you to switch from Windows?
